explanations.answer: A new heaven and a new earth
explanations.explanation: John says, “Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth…” because the first heaven and earth had passed away. I know a little about fresh starts. One night I'm in the back of a junk drawer, and next thing I know an angel has me standing on a cookie planet. But this new is heaven AND earth, friend, so mine looks small.

explanations.answer: A wide desert under a dark sky
explanations.explanation: Nothing in the verse mentions a desert or a dark sky. John says, “Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth…” The passage even says there will be no more night in the city (Revelation 22:5). Nobody's squinting through the dark in this vision, baker.

explanations.answer: An empty sky over deep waters
explanations.explanation: John doesn't see an empty sky. He says he saw “a new heaven and a new earth,” and he adds that the sea was no more. So there are no deep waters in the picture, and the heaven and earth he sees are new. Empty is not the word, baker.

explanations.answer: As a bride adorned for her husband
explanations.explanation: John says the city is prepared “as a bride adorned for her husband.” That fits my work nicely, since the Supper I'm baking for is a marriage supper (Revelation 19:9). I'm not saying I cried into the dough, but the dough is a little salty. A wedding is the picture, friend.

explanations.answer: As a crown set with every jewel
explanations.explanation: Jewels do show up later in this passage, in the city's foundations, so I see why a crown tempted you. But verse 2 says the city is prepared “as a bride adorned for her husband.” There's no crown in that verse. A crown would look great on my counter, though, I'll admit that.

explanations.answer: As a king's house ready for guests
explanations.explanation: Guests are a nice thought, friend, but the verse isn't picturing a house at all. John says the city is prepared “as a bride adorned for her husband.” The picture is a bride getting ready for her husband. I'd bake for that day after day.

True. The loud voice from the throne says, “Behold, the dwelling place of God is with man, and He will dwell with them.” God Himself, right there with His people. I'll be honest, friend, this verse makes my mustache stand straight up.

This one is true, friend, so False slipped past. The loud voice from the throne says, “Behold, the dwelling place of God is with man, and He will dwell with them.” So God's dwelling place is with man. Read it slowly, because there's a lot of good packed into one breath.

The voice says there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, “…for the former things have passed away.” The old things are done, and that's why those four go with them. I love how plain that is. Short line, huge news.
Evil is a fair guess, baker, since death and pain are heavy things. But the voice says “former.” The line reads, “…for the former things have passed away.” It's the old things that are gone.

Hidden would make this a mystery, and this verse is nice and plain. The voice says, “…for the former things have passed away.” The word is “former,” as in the old things. Nothing is being kept secret here, friend.

“Behold, I make all things new.” ALL things, friend. Not some things, not just the top shelf, ALL. I'm a stamper who got made new, so I'm a little biased, but that might be my favorite line in the whole passage.
Great is a word I'd happily use for Him, baker. But the verse says, “Behold, I make all things new.” The word is new. Say it with me, new. ALL things.

Bright fits the city, which shines with the glory of God. But in this verse the One seated on the throne says, “Behold, I make all things new.” The word is new, friend. And it goes with all things, not just some.

explanations.answer: These words are faithful and true
explanations.explanation: The One on the throne says, “Write this down, for these words are faithful and true.” He gives the reason Himself, so we don't have to guess. I write down my recipes, and half of them just say 'more chips.' These words are on a whole different level.

explanations.answer: John might forget what he saw
explanations.explanation: The text never says John might forget. It gives one reason: “for these words are faithful and true.” That's the reason on the page. I think it's plenty, baker.

explanations.answer: The angels want a record of it
explanations.explanation: No angels are asking for a record here, friend. The One on the throne tells John, “Write this down, for these words are faithful and true.” The reason He gives is about the words themselves. I'll stick with the reason the verse gives.
“To the thirsty I will give freely from the spring of the water of life.” Freely, friend. That means given, not sold. All it asks for is thirst, and I have been thirsty for less than this.

The wealthy aren't mentioned in that verse. The One on the throne says, “To the thirsty I will give freely from the spring of the water of life.” Freely means nothing is being charged. A bigger wallet doesn't change a thing at a spring like that.
Priests don't appear in that verse, baker. He says, “To the thirsty I will give freely from the spring of the water of life.” The ones He names are the thirsty. And He gives it freely.

He says the opposite, friend. “The one who overcomes will inherit all things, and I will be his God, and he will be My son.” All things, not a small share. A small share would be me splitting one cookie five ways, and this promise is the whole bakery.

False is the one, and it's a big one. “The one who overcomes will inherit all things…” All things, friend, not a sliver. Then He adds, “I will be his God, and he will be My son.” That's the best part of the promise.

explanations.answer: The cowardly and unbelieving and all liars
explanations.explanation: This part is heavy, so I'll say it plain. He says, “…and all liars, their place will be in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur.” The list starts with the cowardly and unbelieving, and it names more than that. Then He says, “This is the second death.”

explanations.answer: Everyone who lived on the first earth
explanations.explanation: This part is heavy, friend, so let's stick to what it says. The text doesn't say everyone who lived on the first earth. It names the cowardly and unbelieving and abominable and murderers and sexually immoral and sorcerers and idolaters and all liars. Right before that, He promised the overcomer all things.

explanations.answer: Anyone who never saw the new city
explanations.explanation: This part is heavy, so I'll keep it simple. Nothing in the verse says anyone who never saw the city. It names the cowardly and unbelieving and abominable and murderers and sexually immoral and sorcerers and idolaters and all liars. The text says what it says, baker.

The city is “shining with the glory of God.” Later John says the glory of God illuminates the city (Revelation 21:23). No need for a bulb or a box. My stars come from finished cookie boxes, but this city needs none.

The stars light up MY sky, one for every finished cookie box. But the city isn't shining with starlight. The text says it's “shining with the glory of God.” Verse 25 even says there will be no night there, so stars would have nothing to do.

No torches in this verse, friend. The city is “shining with the glory of God.” Verse 23 says the city has no need of sun or moon, because the glory of God illuminates it. The only lamp mentioned is the Lamb Himself.
True. The city has “twelve gates inscribed with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel.” Twelve gates, twelve names. I didn't even have to carry the one.

The names are right there on the gates, friend. John says the city had “twelve gates inscribed with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel.” Twelve gates, twelve tribes. The wall's foundations carry names too, but that's a different set.

“The wall of the city had twelve foundations bearing the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.” Jesus chose twelve of His disciples and called them apostles (Luke 6:13). So the tribes' names are on the gates, and the apostles' names are on the foundations. That's a lot of names for one wall, baker.

Elders do show up elsewhere in Revelation (Revelation 4:4), but not on these foundations. This verse says the foundations bear the names of “the twelve apostles of the Lamb.” The names on the foundations are the apostles', friend.

Prophets aren't named on the foundations here, friend. The text says “the twelve apostles of the Lamb.” The names of the tribes are on the gates, and the apostles' names are on the foundations. Keep those two sets straight and you're golden.

explanations.answer: The Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple
explanations.explanation: John says, “…because the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple.” The Lamb is Jesus (John 1:29). So there's no building to point at. The temple is Them, and I think that's about the best thing a city could have.

explanations.answer: The people worship outside its walls
explanations.explanation: The text puts worship inside the city. Revelation 22:3 says the throne of God and of the Lamb will be within the city, and His servants will worship Him. So nobody is stuck outside the walls. The reason for no temple is that the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple.

explanations.answer: The old temple stayed behind on the old earth
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say a word about an old temple staying behind. It gives the reason itself: the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple. I think that beats any reason I could cook up, friend.
“…the glory of God illuminates the city, and the Lamb is its lamp.” The Lamb is Jesus (John 1:29). So the light comes from God's glory and from the Lamb. Sun and moon can take the day off, baker.
A shield is a good thing to have, but this verse says lamp. John writes, “…the glory of God illuminates the city, and the Lamb is its lamp.” Illuminates is a light word, so a lamp fits.

A crown sounds grand, and I do love grand. But the verse says the Lamb is its lamp. That's what John writes: “…the glory of God illuminates the city, and the Lamb is its lamp.” The city's light comes from the glory of God, friend.

“By its light the nations will walk, and into it the kings of the earth will bring their glory.” The nations walk by the city's light, and the kings bring their glory in. I think that's a lot of people on one street, friend. The street is pure gold, so it'll look good.
Angels are in the passage, friend. There are twelve at the gates. But the verse says, “By its light the nations will walk…” The nations are the ones walking by its light.

Elders aren't named in this verse, baker. John writes, “By its light the nations will walk, and into it the kings of the earth will bring their glory.” The walkers are the nations. The kings bring the glory.

John says the opposite. “Its gates will never be shut at the end of the day, because there will be no night there.” No closing time at all. My bakery has a CLOSED sign I flip every night, and this city doesn't even own one.

False is the one, friend. “Its gates will never be shut at the end of the day, because there will be no night there.” No night, so no closing time. I have a CLOSED sign in my bakery, and this city doesn't need one.

explanations.answer: Those whose names are written in the Lamb's Book of Life
explanations.explanation: The verse says, “…only those whose names are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life.” The Lamb is Jesus (John 1:29). It's about whose names are written down. That's the whole answer, and I love how clear it is.

explanations.answer: Those who carry gold and jewels up to its gates
explanations.explanation: Gold and jewels are all over this city, friend. The street is pure gold, and the foundations are adorned with every kind of precious stone. But the verse says only those whose names are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life enter. Nobody gets in by what they carry.

explanations.answer: Those who were born and raised inside its walls
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say anything about being born or raised inside the walls. It says, “…only those whose names are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life.” Names written there is the answer. Remember that, baker.
The river is “flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb.” So the water of life starts right at the throne. The Lamb is Jesus (John 1:29). I'd follow that river upstream any day, baker.
No garden in that verse, friend. John says the river is “flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb.” The throne is where the water starts. Remember that spot.

John did stand on a mountain, great and high, when the angel showed him the city (Revelation 21:10). But the river doesn't flow from there. John says it's “flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb.” The throne is the source, baker.

On either side of the river stands a tree of life. And that tree has twelve kinds of fruit and a fresh crop each month. A tree that never runs out is my kind of kitchen. I'd just keep walking back to it.
A tree of the knowledge of good and evil stood in Eden (Genesis 2:9), so I see the thought. But the tree by this river is a tree of life. That's what John says. Life, friend.
Peace is something I'd plant a whole orchard of, friend. But the verse says, “a tree of life.” The word is life. John says one stands on either side of the river.

John says it's more than once a year. The tree is “bearing twelve kinds of fruit and yielding a fresh crop for each month.” That's a new crop every month, baker. Once a year? My ovens do more work than that before breakfast.
False is the one. The tree is “bearing twelve kinds of fruit and yielding a fresh crop for each month.” A fresh crop every month, not once a year. My ovens would be jealous, friend.
“No longer will there be any curse.” None at all, friend. And the throne of God and of the Lamb will be within the city, so His servants are worshiping Him right there. That's a good place to be.
The gates are still there, baker. Twelve of them, and they will never be shut at the end of the day (Revelation 21:25). The thing that's gone is the curse. “No longer will there be any curse.”

Kings are still around, friend. John says the kings of the earth will bring their glory into the city (Revelation 21:24). The thing that won't be there is the curse. “No longer will there be any curse.”
True. John says, “They will see His face, and His name will be on their foreheads.” God's servants will see His face. I've been waiting a good while to hear a line like that, baker.
This one is true, friend, so False slipped past. John says, “They will see His face, and His name will be on their foreheads.” God's servants will see His face. It's right there in the verse.
John says, “…they will reign forever and ever.” No end date at all. I've been given a lot of deadlines in my day, and this is the first line that doesn't have one. Forever and ever, friend.

A thousand years comes up earlier in Revelation (Revelation 20:4), but this verse doesn't use it. John says, “…they will reign forever and ever.” There's no end point given here. Forever and ever, baker.
The text doesn't give an end point like that, friend. It says, “…they will reign forever and ever.” No next age is named. Forever and ever is the answer, and it's a good one.
